name: York KAMPground
note: Big open I-80 stopover at exit 353 in York (214 Naomi Rd), restaurants and shopping within walking distance: 139 pull-through sites, 30/50-amp. Water/electric sites $30-35 and full hookups $50-55 a night plus tax; weekly and monthly rates. Restrooms with showers, laundry. Online booking (ResNexus). RV Life 4*/$$. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: yorkkampground.com live with a rates page (W/E $30/$35, FHU $50/$55 per night plus tax, read 2026-10-02) and ResNexus online booking; RV Life 4* $$ over 96 reviews; Google listing at the pin with phone (read 2026-10-02); transient interstate park, nightly rates first
waterfront_evidence: satellite (Esri, 600 m frame) at 40.8242,-97.5928: gravel pull-through rows on open ground south of the office between motels and a field; a marshy pond lies ~200 m east behind a brush strip; default down - not waterfront

name: Little Rivers Edge RV Park
note: Newer small RV park a mile west of Syracuse on a gravel road above the Little Nemaha River: about 14 sites with 20/30/50-amp electric, picnic table and fire pit; two water hydrants, no sewer (dump stations a mile away). Walk-in tent areas. Daily, weekly and monthly rates; online booking (Firefly). RV Life 4.5*/$$. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: littleriversedge.com live (sites, hookups, online reservations via Firefly, read 2026-10-02); RV Life 4.5* $$ over 2 reviews, Google 4.9 over 24 with phone (read 2026-10-02) - thin but every signal positive; satellite shows a finished gravel loop of back-in pads
waterfront_evidence: satellite (Esri, 500 m frame) at 40.6537,-96.2095: the gravel site loop sits on an open rise south of the Little Nemaha, whose bends pass ~60-120 m north and east of the pads behind grass slope and a tree line; the operator's 'overlooks the river' is marketing and the sightline can't be confirmed through the trees; default down - not waterfront

name: Beaver Crossing Park Campground
note: Village of Beaver Crossing campground in the town park, entered at 1025 Elk St by the ball field and playground. Electric and water (warm months) at the RV sites; first come, first served, suggested donation $10 a night paid in the box at the entrance or at the village clerk's office. No dump station. RV Life 4.5*/$. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: beavercrossingvillage.com Parks & Recreation page (read 2026-10-02): village-run RV campground, electric + water, FCFS, $10/night donation; RV Life 4.5* over 36 reviews (24 sites); Google 'Beaver Crossing City Park Camping Area' 4.9 over 12 at the pin. Local government - no price/star gate. A local-pass miss found by the private list (RV Life types it commercial)
waterfront_evidence: satellite (Esri, 500 m frame) at 40.7764,-97.2775: the camping area is gravel by the Elk St entrance between the playground and the ball fields in the village park; only a narrow drainage channel runs past; not waterfront

name: Auburn RV Park (City of Auburn)
note: City of Auburn RV park at the Auburn Recreation Complex (419 Q St), a loop of gravel pads in the trees beside the ball fields and trail. $20 a night, reservations through the city; open April 1 - October 31 (water off in a freeze), 10-night limit, restrooms and a dump station. RV Life 4*/$. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: auburn.ne.gov/rv-park/ (read 2026-10-02): city-run, $20/night, reservations, Apr-Oct, 10-night limit, dump station; RV Life 4* over 25 reviews (12 sites); Google 'Auburn City Recreation Complex' 4.7 over 95 with the city phone.
